name: Turbinate reduction
summary: Surgery that shrinks enlarged inferior turbinates to improve nasal breathing; a functional procedure with many techniques and limited high-quality comparisons.
lead: Turbinate reduction is a group of surgical procedures that reduce the size of the inferior turbinates, the mucosa-covered structures on the side walls of the nasal cavity, to relieve nasal obstruction. It is often combined with septoplasty or rhinoplasty because enlargement can occur on the side opposite a deviated septum, described as compensatory hypertrophy.
claims: Turbinate reduction should be avoided at all costs because of empty nose syndrome.
If turbinates are truly oversized, reduction is the only thing that fixes the blockage.

name: Nasal valve repair
summary: Functional surgery to widen or support the narrowest part of the nasal airway when it collapses; the literature is mostly case series with improvements reported.
lead: Nasal valve repair refers to surgical techniques that treat obstruction caused by compromise of the nasal valve, the narrow region of the airway at the junction of the upper lateral cartilage, septum and turbinate. It is a form of functional rhinoplasty.

name: Ultrasonic (piezo) rhinoplasty
summary: Nose surgery that reshapes bone with piezoelectric ultrasonic tools instead of chisels and rasps; evidence is thin and mostly descriptive.
lead: Ultrasonic rhinoplasty is a way of performing the bone work of rhinoplasty using piezoelectric instruments designed for the purpose. A 2023 review of ultrasonic rhinoplasty and septoplasty states that the instruments allow precise osteotomies under direct visual control after an open or extended closed approach, as well as ostectomies and rhinosculpture, and that they preserve bone stability by not damaging support structures and avoiding unwanted fractures.

name: Preservation rhinoplasty
summary: Nose surgery that lowers or reshapes the bridge while keeping the natural dorsal structure intact rather than cutting a hump off; popular among surgeons, with mostly case-series evidence.
lead: Preservation rhinoplasty, also called dorsal preservation rhinoplasty, refers to techniques that address a dorsal hump or the nasal profile by repositioning rather than removing the natural dorsum. A 2020 review notes a rekindled interest in dorsal preservation as an alternative to conventional hump resection, with claims of superior functional and aesthetic results, and describes mobilising the osseocartilaginous vault as a single unit to avoid disrupting natural structure.

name: Revision rhinoplasty
summary: A second (or later) operation to correct problems from a previous nose job; revision rates are documented and the procedure often needs grafts.
lead: Revision rhinoplasty, or secondary rhinoplasty, is a nose operation performed after a previous rhinoplasty to address aesthetic or functional problems. A general reference gives 5 to 20 percent as the share of primary operations needing a second procedure and lists typical problems such as breathing deficits, asymmetry, collapse, a hanging columella, a pinched tip and a scooped nose. A study of a plastic surgery group practice examined cosmetic rhinoplasty revision rates and risk factors for dissatisfaction.
claims: A nose tip that relapses after surgery can be caused by insufficient support from a recessed maxilla.
A dropped tip may need only a minor closed procedure rather than a full revision.

name: Alar base reduction (alarplasty)
summary: Surgery that trims the nostril flare; usually done alongside a nose job, with little trial evidence of its own.
lead: Alar base reduction, usually called alarplasty, is a cosmetic nasal surgery that narrows the width of the nostril flare or the base of the nose by removing small wedges of tissue at the nostril rim or the alar-facial junction. It is performed either on its own or together with rhinoplasty, and surgeons describe it as one of several tools for correcting nostril size and shape.
claims: Narrowing the alar base noticeably improves a wide nose
The change may be too small to justify surgery for some faces

name: Tip plasty / cartilage grafting
summary: Surgical reshaping of the nose tip with sutures and cartilage grafts; an established rhinoplasty step backed by technique papers, not large trials.
lead: Tip plasty (nasal tip refinement) is the part of rhinoplasty that reshapes, repositions or supports the nasal tip, using cartilage sutures, cartilage excision or cartilage grafts. It is generally described as one of the technically more demanding parts of nose surgery.

name: Rib cartilage graft rhinoplasty
summary: Uses the patient's own rib cartilage for big structural rebuilds of the nose; supported by surgical case series.
lead: Rib (costal) cartilage graft rhinoplasty is a form of nose surgery in which cartilage harvested from the patient's own ribs is carved into grafts to support or build up the nose. It is used when a large amount of structural material is needed, for example in major dorsal reconstruction or revision surgery.

name: Silicone/Gore-Tex nasal implant
summary: Synthetic bridge implants for low noses, long used in Asian rhinoplasty, with cartilage as the main alternative.
lead: Silicone and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (Gore-Tex) nasal implants are synthetic (alloplastic) materials placed in the nose, most often to raise a low nasal bridge. They are an alternative to the patient's own cartilage and are particularly associated in the literature with augmentation rhinoplasty in Asian patients.
claims: Many Asian nose jobs look "fake"

name: Septal extension graft
summary: A cartilage graft that extends the septum to control nose-tip length, projection and rotation; established technique with growing comparative data.
lead: A septal extension graft is a piece of cartilage, usually from the septum, attached to the end of the nasal septum in rhinoplasty to control the position, length, projection and rotation of the nasal tip. It is used particularly in patients with weak lower lateral cartilages.

name: PDO nose thread lift
summary: Absorbable threads placed in the nose to lift bridge or tip without surgery; very little published evidence.
lead: A PDO nose thread lift is a minimally invasive, non-surgical rhinoplasty procedure in which absorbable polydioxanone (PDO) threads are inserted under the skin of the nose, sometimes together with filler, to raise the bridge or tip.

name: Botox nose tip lift
summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the muscle that pulls the nasal tip down; a temporary, off-label tip lift with no published trials behind it.
lead: A Botox nose tip lift is a cosmetic procedure in which botulinum toxin is injected into the depressor septi nasi muscle, a small muscle that pulls the nasal tip and the base of the nostrils downward, in order to relax it and allow the tip of the nose to sit slightly higher. It is sometimes grouped with other non-surgical nose treatments and is described by its proponents as a short-term alternative to surgery for a drooping tip, particularly one that drops further when a person smiles or speaks.

name: Nose contouring makeup
summary: Shading and highlighting to make the nose look slimmer; purely optical, reversible and untested in studies.
lead: Nose contouring is a makeup technique in which a darker shade is applied along the sides of the nose and a lighter shade on the bridge or tip, with the aim of making the nose look slimmer, straighter or more defined through light and shadow. It is a specific application of contouring, defined as using cosmetics to define, enhance and sculpt facial structure.

name: Nasal taping at night
summary: Micropore or kinesiology tape worn on the nose overnight for a slimmer look; surgeons say any effect vanishes when the tape comes off.
lead: Nasal taping is a social-media trend in which people apply adhesive tape, commonly micropore paper tape or kinesiology tape, across the bridge and sides of the nose for several hours or overnight in an attempt to create a slimmer, more lifted or more defined nose. It is often marketed as a non-surgical mini nose job.
claims: Taping overnight slims or lifts the nose
Repeated taping gradually remodels the cartilage
Taping improves nasal breathing and sleep

name: Nose-lifting or slimming massage
summary: Daily nose rubbing or pinching claimed to slim or lift the nose; no studies have tested it.
lead: Nose-lifting or slimming massage refers to the practice of pressing, pinching or rubbing the nose, often daily, with the aim of making it narrower, higher-bridged or more lifted. It is described in beauty and appearance communities as a no-cost, non-surgical option.

name: Nose exercises (nose yoga)
summary: Nostril flaring and nose scrunching routines claimed to reshape the nose; no studies have tested them.
lead: Nose exercises, sometimes called nose yoga, are routines of flaring the nostrils, wiggling or scrunching the nose, or pressing on the tip, promoted as a way to strengthen nasal muscles and change the shape of the nostrils or nasal tip. They belong to the wider category of facial exercise or face yoga.

name: Buteyko breathing
summary: A breathing-retraining method built around nasal, reduced breathing; asthma trials show modest symptom effects and none test it for looks.
lead: The Buteyko method is a breathing retraining system developed by Ukrainian physiologist Konstantin Buteyko in the Soviet Union in the 1950s. Its three principles are nasal breathing, reduced breathing, and relaxation, and it is based on the theory that chronic over-breathing (hyperventilation) causes or worsens conditions such as asthma.
claims: Breathing less raises CO2 and calms anxiety
It improves asthma more than medication
Damage from mouth breathing makes nighttime nasal breathing hard, prompting mouth taping

name: Rhinophyma laser / surgery
summary: Medical removal of the thickened, bulbous nasal tissue of advanced rosacea, usually by CO2 laser or surgical shaving; a recognised clinical procedure, not a looksmaxxing invention.
lead: Rhinophyma is a condition in which the nose becomes large and bulbous through thickening of the skin, enlargement of sebaceous glands and fibrous change. It is most often regarded as an advanced stage of rosacea and is most common in older men of European ancestry . Colloquial names include "whiskey nose" and "gin blossom", although the link with alcohol has not been established as causal .

name: Nasofrontal / nasolabial angle theory
summary: Profile-angle metrics borrowed from rhinoplasty and orthodontics that forums use to score noses and brow-to-nose transitions.
lead: The nasofrontal angle and the nasolabial angle are two measurements of the nose in side view. The nasofrontal angle sits at the nasion between the line along the forehead (nasion to glabella) and the line along the nasal dorsum, while the nasolabial angle is formed between the columella and the line from the subnasale to the upper lip .
claims: A good nasofrontal angle is a key part of an attractive side profile.
Brow-ridge implants or brow augmentation can improve a poor nasofrontal angle.
The nasolabial angle should be ideal, and its surgical correction or jaw movement is part of an ascension plan.

name: Rhinoplasty simulation apps
summary: Morphing and 3D-imaging tools that preview how a nose might look after surgery; used by clinics and by prospective patients, with outcomes that are not guaranteed.
lead: Rhinoplasty simulation refers to software that predicts or illustrates how a nose might look after surgery. Surgical references describe 3D simulations and 3D cameras that capture and analyse the nose, allow modifications, and help surgeon and patient understand the anatomy and preview a potential result .

name: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY)
summary: Do-it-yourself filing or striking of a nasal bump; no published studies or sources support it, while surgical literature describes dorsal hump reduction as a surgeon-performed procedure.
lead: Dorsal hump rasping (DIY) is the name given to attempts to lower a bump on the nasal bridge at home by filing or striking it. The sources consulted for this wiki do not document how common the practice is or describe its methods.

name: Nasal splint after rhinoplasty
summary: A rigid or semi-rigid cover, sometimes with internal stents, that holds the reshaped nose still while it heals.
lead: A nasal splint is a protective device placed over or inside the nose after surgery. After rhinoplasty, the surgeon typically applies tape and a custom-shaped splint to keep the nose still while the incisions heal, and the dressing is removed about one week after the procedure .

name: Nasal irrigation
summary: Saline rinsing of the nose, used for congestion and sinus symptoms; looksmaxxing interest centres on clearing congestion, with no studies of its effect on nose appearance.
lead: Nasal irrigation, also called nasal lavage or neti pot use, is a hygiene and medical practice that rinses the nasal cavity with a saline solution to remove mucus and debris . It originated in Ayurvedic practice in India, where jala neti is traditionally part of daily personal hygiene .

name: Lip flip (Botox)
summary: Botox in the upper lip muscle to roll the lip out; temporary, with only small studies behind it.
lead: A lip flip is a cosmetic procedure in which small amounts of botulinum toxin type A are injected into the muscle around the mouth, the orbicularis oris, along the upper lip border. Practitioners describe the aim as relaxing the muscle so the upper lip rolls slightly outward and upward, showing a little more of the pink lip without adding volume .
claims: A lip flip can make a thin upper lip look fuller and change facial proportions.
The effect is temporary and reversible.
The injection can be self-administered at home.

name: Lip lift (bullhorn / subnasal)
summary: Surgery that shortens a long philtrum by removing skin under the nose; permanent, with the scar as the main trade-off.
lead: A lip lift is a surgical procedure that shortens the vertical distance between the base of the nose and the upper lip by removing a strip of skin, raising the lip and showing more of the vermilion, the pink part of the lip. In the subnasal or "bullhorn" version the incision is hidden under the nose .
claims: Shortening the philtrum by a few millimetres improves several ratios at once.
The scar can be hidden.
Many people who want a lip lift need filler or fat grafting instead.

name: Fat grafting lips
summary: Your own fat injected into the lips; semi-permanent, with partial reabsorption reported.
lead: Lip fat grafting, also called autologous fat transfer, moves a person's own fat, usually taken by liposuction from another body area, into the lips to add volume. Wikipedia describes it as one of the better options for a semi-permanent result, with possible lumps or scarring .

name: Lip implants (Permalip, Gore-Tex)
summary: Permanent solid inserts (Gore-Tex or silicone) for lip volume; durable but with extrusion and migration risks.
lead: Lip implants are solid, permanent inserts placed in the lips to increase volume. Two materials are most discussed: expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE, sold as Gore-Tex and similar products) and solid silicone (Permalip) .

name: Lip reduction surgery
summary: Surgery that trims thick lips; mostly studied for medical conditions rather than cosmetic goals.
lead: Lip reduction surgery, or reduction cheiloplasty, removes tissue from the lips to make them smaller. It is used for cosmetic reasons and for medical conditions such as macrocheilia from vascular malformations, granulomatous cheilitis and Van der Woude syndrome .
claims: Very full lips can hurt facial harmony and may merit reduction.

name: V-Y advancement / vermilion advancement
summary: Flap surgery that moves pink lip tissue; mostly reconstructive, with little cosmetic research.
lead: Vermilion advancement is a group of surgical techniques that move or advance the pink lip tissue, the vermilion, to rebuild or enlarge it. In the literature it is mostly a reconstructive method, for example after tumour removal from the lip, while in cosmetic surgery it is discussed as a way to increase pink lip show .

name: Lip blushing (cosmetic tattoo)
summary: A cosmetic tattoo that tints the lips semi-permanently; documented mostly through case reports of reactions, with no appearance trials.
lead: Lip blushing is a form of cosmetic tattooing, also called permanent makeup or micropigmentation, in which pigment is placed in the skin of the lips to add or even out color and soften the lip border . In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a semi-permanent alternative to tinted lip balm for people who describe their lip color as uneven or pale .
claims: A lip blush tattoo can permanently even out uneven lip color.
If it looks fake on a man, the result is ruined.
Lip color is a key contrasting feature of the face.
